patch_resolves_note: The staged `patch.diff` does not apply to the workspace checkout left by Stage 01, so Stage 04 used the authoritative `n132/arvo:16531-fix` image for fixed-side evidence. On that fixed image the original PoC runs clean and still reaches `second_decode_stop` genuinely with `size_mod_chr == 0` and `token_export.token_len == second_decode_stop.size_bytes == 10`.

root_cause_criterion.criterion: Immediately before `const Chr * stop = reinterpret_cast<const Chr *>(in0 + size);`, a positive `size` must describe a whole number of `Chr` elements so the `++in` loop can reach its boundary.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the positive-size wide-decoder boundary with an odd byte count (`size_mod_chr == 1`) and still enters the loop. The fixed original reaches the same source event with `size_mod_chr == 0`, so the stop pointer is reachable by `++in`.

nodes.description: At the crashing positive-size decode call, `stop` is the raw byte-end address `in0 + size`, so the loop compares a 2-byte-stride `Chr *` against an unaligned byte boundary.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `second_decode_stop.stop_addr == second_decode_stop.requested_end_addr` at the crashing decode call.

nodes.description: At the sink loop, `in` has advanced strictly past the caller-requested slice end `in0 + size`, so `out.append(*in)` dereferences beyond the requested span on the path that continues to the ASan heap overread.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `second_decode_overread.read_addr > second_decode_overread.requested_end_addr` on every post-stop iteration, including the final dereference before ASan reports the heap-buffer-overflow.

edges.relation: The exported misspelling span length is passed unchanged as the positive-size argument of the second `DecodeDirect<unsigned short>::decode()` call.
edges.evidence: The frozen traces record `token_export.token_len == second_decode_stop.size_bytes` on both versions (5 on the vulnerable crash, 10 on the fixed original).

edges.relation: The same unreachable `stop` pointer computed at the positive-size boundary is the pointer later compared against `in` during the post-stop loop iterations.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `second_decode_stop.stop_addr == second_decode_overread.stop_addr` across the first post-stop dereference.
